question: Do the genotypes differ in sag and rebound when voltage and excursion are matched?
design: Current clamp, layer II/III pyramidal neurons, WT/HT/KO from littermates in the same slice batches; hold every cell at one common potential (bias current), then step to the same peak potential (current scaled per cell from the measured Rin) at two step durations; report absolute sag, sag fraction and rebound.
controls: Same protocol after 2 or 3 holding potentials; series resistance and bridge balance monitored; spontaneously spiking cells not excluded but reported
readout: Absolute and fractional sag, rebound, Rin, Vrest, tau at each matched condition
unit_and_replication: Animal as unit (one value per animal, mixed model); cells listed; HT kept separate from WT
decision_it_changes: If differences vanish: HY1 (recruitment); if they persist: go to X2

question: Is Ih different in amount or gating?
design: Voltage clamp in the same neurons with blockers of other currents; measure Ih amplitude, activation V1/2, slope, kinetics, and tail current; same cells as X1 when possible.
controls: Time-matched run-down control (PMID39548079 reports about 17 percent run-down); Rin check before and after
readout: Ih density (per capacitance), V1/2, slope, tau
decision_it_changes: Different Ih opens HY3 (X6); same Ih supports HY1

question: Which conductance explains the higher Rin and depolarised rest?
design: Add Kv7 (XE991-sensitive) and leak/Kir subtraction in the same cells; ZD7288 sensitive part separated by sequential application.
controls: Vehicle time control; blockers in WT as well
readout: Rin, Vrest, sensitive current by genotype
decision_it_changes: Names the primary membrane conductance; separates Kv7 from other leak before any lever

question: What does an Ih block do to the cell?
design: Acute ZD7288 and a second blocker, each alone, bath, in WT/HT/KO neurons; sag, rebound, Rin, Vrest, firing, AP height; test for sodium-current engagement in a voltage-clamp subset.
controls: Vehicle; wash-out; the same measurement under Kv7 and T-type arms run separately; normalising Vrest by bias current as a second arm
readout: Cell effect, with engagement demonstrated (sag gone) before burst reading
decision_it_changes: Distinguishes HCN contribution to sag from any burst effect

question: Does the cell effect carry to the burst?
design: In bursting KO slices record bursts before and after each X4 arm, with cell recordings in the same slice; non-specific suppression control (evoked fEPSP in WT, AP height, viability).
controls: Slices exposed for matched times; d-APV at a matched reduction as a reference (NMDA package)
readout: Burst frequency and propagation; cell variables
decision_it_changes: Support, no benefit or worsening; a worsening is not read as compensation until compartment and off-target effects are examined

question: Only if X2 differs: is it surface, isoform or position?
design: Surface HCN1/HCN2 and TRIP8b isoforms in neuron-deleted cortex; soma versus dendrite labelling; the FLNa decoy as a tool only after this; lipid-domain read-out only if surface and gating disagree.
decision_it_changes: Chooses between trafficking, lipid and gating explanations
